title: Thévenin, maximum power transfer and superposition
goal: Replace a network by its Thévenin equivalent, find the load that takes the most power, and add up the effects of two sources one at a time.
theory: Seen from two terminals, any linear network of sources and resistors behaves like one source V_th in series with one resistance R_th. V_th is the open-circuit voltage; R_th is the resistance looking back in with the sources turned off (voltage sources shorted).
The power in a load R_L is P = V_th²·R_L / (R_th + R_L)². It peaks when R_L = R_th, where the load gets V_th / 2 and P_max = V_th² / (4·R_th).
Superposition: in a linear circuit the response to several sources is the sum of the responses to each source alone.

prelab.label: V_th of 12 V, R1 = 1 kΩ, R2 = 2 kΩ (open circuit)
Superposition node: 12 V via 1 kΩ, 5 V via 2 kΩ, 1 kΩ to ground

procedure: Load the reference build. RL is a decade resistor box across the network's output (column 12); M1 measures its voltage.
Set RL very high (9.9 MΩ) and record the open-circuit voltage: that is V_th.
Run the load sweep: the lab steps RL from 200 Ω to 10 kΩ and records V_L each time; P = V_L² / R_L is plotted against the theory curve.
Find the R_L of maximum power and compare with R_th.
Superposition (columns 40–46): measure the node with both sources, then think: what would each source alone give?

checks.label: Load voltage at R_L = R_th is V_th / 2
